tasks.task: Remove partition walls and framing
tasks.scope: Demolish non-structural partition walls, internal framing, and stud work. Debris loaded into skip bins. Maintain exclusion zone below active demolition face. Check for hidden services or asbestos before each cut.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker on ladder or elevated platform during wall removal or cuts
Hidden services struck — electrical, water, or gas lines cut accidentally before location confirmed
Struck by falling debris — wall section or frame component detaches unexpectedly
Nail or fastener puncture wound — stepping on or handling debris with exposed fixings
tasks.dominant_hazard: Dust inhalation — silica or asbestos dust from cutting or demolition not suppressed
controls: Wet-cut all partition wall sections and studs. Use water spray to suppress dust continuously during cutting. No dry breakout permitted.
Check for hidden services (power, water, gas) at each cut point using thermal imaging, utility locator, or architect plan before power saw or reciprocating saw starts.
Wear organic vapour + particulate respirator (P2 cartridge + organic vapour cartridge per SDS) during all dry debris handling or re-entry to dust zone.
Wear eye protection, heavy-duty cut-resistant gloves, and steel-capped boots during wall removal and debris handling.
Load debris into skip bin from platform or ground level only. Do not throw from height. Segregate asbestos or asbestos-suspect material into separate skip or sealed bag immediately.
Use harness and lanyard (anchor to fixed structure above, tested safe for load) when cutting from ladder or elevated platform above 2 m. Do not work alone.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not load debris from height until: exclusion zone is confirmed clear of personnel, skip bin position is stable and level, and wet suppression or dust containment is in place
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet suppression system fails, water spray stops, or dry cutting occurs — do not resume until water supply is restored and dust has settled
🛑 STOP WORK if: hidden service is struck, identified, or suspected (electrical outlet, pipe, conduit) — isolate immediately, tell site supervisor, do not touch or cut further
🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion zone is breached by unauthorised personnel, debris escapes containment, or air quality cannot be maintained
admin: Obtain and display Asbestos Removal Permit (if Class A asbestos confirmed) before any licensed removal work starts.
Arrange independent air monitoring during all Class A asbestos removal work. Provide results to SafeWork NSW within prescribed timeframe.
Brief all site personnel on exclusion zone boundaries, RPE requirements, and stop-work triggers before work starts.
Maintain disposal certificates for all asbestos waste. Arrange licensed asbestos waste contractor for removal and burial at approved facility.
Provide Site Induction and SWMS walkthrough to all workers before tool issue. Confirm understanding in writing.
ppe: Organic vapour + particulate respirator (P2 cartridge + organic vapour cartridge per SDS) — wear during cutting, demolition, and dry debris handling
eye protection— during cutting, demolition, and debris loading
Steel-capped boots — on site always during demolition
hi-viz shirt or vest— during all work in exclusion zone
High-visibility vest — for visibility below active demolition face

monitoring.critical_control: Verify water spray is active and continuous during all cutting. Check dust visible in air — if present, stop and increase water pressure.
monitoring.frequency: Before each cut and continuous during cutting
monitoring.evidence: Water supply connected and flowing visibly; air quality observed clear; exclusion zone barricade remains intact; no personnel without RPE in zone

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove partition walls and framing
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove partition walls and framing per SWMS

tasks.task: Engage licensed asbestos removalist and establish containment
tasks.scope: Confirm Class B licence holder engaged, containment barriers erected around ACM areas (vinyl floor tiles and pipe lagging), method statement and site-specific control plan approved before removal work commences.
hazards: Asbestos fibres released during containment setup — inadequate barriers or poor installation
Class B licence holder not verified or not current at commencement
Containment plan not tailored to site layout — vinyl floor tiles and pipe lagging not fully enclosed
Method statement and control plan not approved in writing before work starts
tasks.dominant_hazard: Asbestos fibres released during containment setup — inadequate barriers or poor installation
controls: Verify Class B licence holder is current on SafeWork NSW register before any work commences — obtain licence copy and expiry date.

Obtain written site-specific method statement and containment plan from licensed removalist — must identify vinyl floor tiles and pipe lagging locations, containment type, and fibre release control measures.
Confirm containment barriers (polyethylene sheeting minimum 200 micron) are installed around all ACM work areas — seal all seams and penetrations with duct tape before removal begins.
Erect exclusion zone minimum 2 m radius around containment barriers — barricade with hazard tape and no-entry signs.
Establish negative pressure containment if removal method produces visible dust — HEPA extraction unit running continuously during and for 30 min after barrier removal.
Confirm method statement includes fibre suppression protocol — wet method, low-velocity air extraction, or encapsulation — before setup commences.
Conduct air monitoring point locations and baseline read before containment is breached — licensed air monitor or external NATA lab assigned.
Brief all site workers on containment location, exclusion zone boundary, and no-unauthorised-entry rule — sign-off sheet completed.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not breach containment or start removal until: licensed removalist confirms written method statement and site-specific plan signed by Site Supervisor, and containment barriers visually inspected and sealed by Supervisor.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove containment barriers until: post-removal air monitoring completed and result confirms fibre count within safe threshold — documented by air monitor or NATA lab.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: Class B licence holder cannot be verified as current on SafeWork NSW register before work starts.
🛑 STOP WORK if: containment barriers show visible gaps, loose seams, or damaged sheeting during setup — do not breach until repaired and re-inspected.
🛑 STOP WORK if: method statement does not name fibre suppression method or does not match site ACM locations (vinyl floor tiles and pipe lagging).
admin: Obtain SafeWork NSW asbestos removal notification receipt and confirm lodged before work start — retain for records.
Obtain written method statement and site-specific containment plan from licensed removalist — review and sign off before commencement.
Assign licensed air monitor or arrange NATA air monitoring lab — baseline and post-removal readings recorded.
Complete site induction and containment zone briefing — attendance sheet retained.
tell occupants and adjacent tenants of asbestos removal activity and expected duration — written notice or confirmation.
ppe: Fitted P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) (organic vapour cartridge if wet suppression chemical used) — supplied by licensed removalist.
Disposable protective coveralls (Type 5/6 minimum) — supplied by licensed removalist.

monitoring.critical_control: Licensed removalist verifies Class B registration and containment barrier seal integrity daily.
monitoring.frequency: before commencement; daily during containment setup; before barrier breach
monitoring.evidence: Licence copy on site; visual inspection sign-off; method statement and containment plan dated and signed; air monitoring baseline recorded.

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

tasks.task: Remove asbestos-containing materials under Class B licence
tasks.scope: Licensed removalist to remove and bag vinyl floor tiles and pipe lagging ACM. Containment maintained throughout. Waste transported and disposed at licensed facility per asbestos waste protocol.
hazards: Asbestos fibre inhalation — containment breach, poor work practice, or inadequate respiratory protection
Cross-contamination of non-ACM areas — dust or waste transported outside controlled zone
Waste not transported or disposed at licensed facility — illegal dumping or mixing with general waste
Worker exposure during bagging or loading — gloves torn, respiratory equipment not fitted correctly
tasks.dominant_hazard: Asbestos fibre inhalation — containment breach, poor work practice, or inadequate respiratory protection
controls: Establish negative pressure containment enclosure around work area before removal starts — check plastic sheeting sealed at all edges and verify air extraction ducting connected to HEPA filter unit.
Wear respiratory protection rated for asbestos fibres (P3 or equivalent per SDS) and check facepiece seal before each removal task — remove and refit if seal is broken or damaged.
Wet all asbestos materials with water mist before cutting, lifting, or bagging — do not allow dry breakout or disturbance of settled dust.
Bag all asbestos waste in marked asbestos waste bags as removed — seal each bag immediately after filling and wipe exterior with damp cloth.
Transport all sealed asbestos waste in covered vehicle direct to licensed disposal facility — do not stop or transfer to other containers en route.
Monitor air extraction unit HEPA filter pressure during work — stop work if filter indicator shows saturation or airflow drops.
Decontaminate work area using HEPA vacuum only — do not sweep or use compressed air.
Remove contaminated work clothing in designated change room before leaving site — do not transport home or mix with general laundry.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start removal until: negative pressure containment enclosure is complete, all seals verified, air extraction unit tested, and removalist Class B licence checked by site supervisor.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not transport waste until: all asbestos bags sealed and exterior wiped, and licensed disposal facility booking confirmed with disposal facility certificate on site.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: containment enclosure plastic is torn, cracked, or unsealed — repair or re-establish enclosure before work resumes.
🛑 STOP WORK if: air extraction unit fails, HEPA filter saturates, or negative pressure is lost — do not disturb ACM until ventilation is restored and verified.
🛑 STOP WORK if: respiratory protection facepiece is damaged, not fitted correctly, or worn worker reports discomfort — verify fit and replace equipment before work resumes.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any asbestos material is exposed outside containment zone — establish additional containment and decontaminate affected area using HEPA vacuum.
admin: Obtain asbestos removal permit from relevant council or authority where required — copy held on site.
Brief removalist and all site personnel on containment procedure, waste transport route, and disposal facility contact details before work commences.
Maintain register of all asbestos waste bags removed — record bag number, material type, weight, and disposal facility receipt.
Obtain licensed disposal facility disposal certificate upon completion — file on site.
ppe: P3 respiratory protection (or equivalent per SDS) — fitted correctly and checked before each work cycle.
Disposable full-body protective suit — Tyvek or equivalent, worn over all work clothing.
steel-capped footwear— do not wear fabric shoes.
Eye protection — glasses or eye protection, worn always in containment zone.

monitoring.critical_control: Check negative pressure enclosure seal and air extraction unit HEPA filter pressure continuous during work.
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during removal — visual check every 15 minutes, HEPA filter pressure checked before each bag sealed.
monitoring.evidence: Air extraction unit pressure gauge reading recorded, visual log of enclosure integrity, waste register with disposal certificates.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove asbestos-containing materials under Class
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove asbestos-containing materials under Class per SWMS

tasks.task: Disconnect electrical, data and mechanical services
tasks.scope: Licensed electrical contractor to isolate and disconnect power, data cabling, and mechanical services. Mechanical contractor to isolate HVAC, water, and gas connections. All terminations capped and isolated points confirmed safe.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.6 — Work in or adjacent to energised electrical installation
hazards: Electric shock from live circuits — isolation not complete or power re-energised during work
Gas line not isolated — pressurised gas release or inhalation hazard
Water line rupture or flooding — inadequate capping or pressure release
Stored energy release — mechanical springs or compressed systems not de-energised before disconnect
tasks.dominant_hazard: Electric shock from live circuits — isolation not complete or power re-energised during work
controls: Verify all circuits at distribution board are isolated and tagged by licensed electrician before any disconnection work starts.
Test each circuit with a live circuit detector at point of work to confirm de-energisation before disconnection.
Cap all disconnected electrical terminals with insulated caps immediately after disconnection.
Isolate mechanical energy sources (springs, compressed air, stored pressure) by depressurising, de-tensioning, or physically locking before any disconnection.
Release water pressure in lines by opening lowest drain point before disconnection; cap all open water connections.
Tag all isolated points with dated isolation tag identifying circuit, service type, and isolating worker.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not disconnect electrical terminals until: licensed electrician has tested circuit with live detector and confirmed de-energisation at point of work
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not disconnect mechanical services until: stored energy has been released, depressurised, or de-tensioned and isolation confirmed by responsible contractor
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: live circuit detector indicates live voltage at any point marked for disconnection
🛑 STOP WORK if: gas line cannot be isolated or depressurised before disconnection, or pressure release point cannot be safely accessed
🛑 STOP WORK if: water line pressure cannot be released or flooding risk is identified
admin: Mechanical contractor to complete isolation checklist for HVAC, water, and gas before disconnection.
Photograph all isolation tags and capped terminals for site record.
Toolbox talk to cover isolation sequence, test procedure, and re-energisation prohibition before work starts.

monitoring.critical_control: Live circuit detector confirms zero voltage at each terminal before disconnection.
monitoring.frequency: Before each circuit disconnection
monitoring.evidence: Isolation and test sheet signed by licensed electrician; dated isolation tags on all capped points

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Disconnect electrical, data and mechanical
responsibility.WKR: Perform Disconnect electrical, data and mechanical per SWMS

tasks.task: Remove fixed joinery and built-in cabinetry
tasks.scope: Disconnect and remove all fixed desks, cabinetry, shelving, and joinery. Load onto skip bins via loading dock. Underlying substrate exposed for inspection.
hazards: Hand or foot crush injury — items tipping or shifting during removal or lowering
Back strain or muscle injury — heavy lifting of desks or cabinetry without mechanical aid
Fall from height — worker standing on unstable joinery or storage to access fixings
Object strike to foot or leg — dropped cabinetry or fasteners during disconnection
tasks.dominant_hazard: Hand or foot crush injury — items tipping or shifting during removal or lowering
controls: Support each cabinet or desk with adjustable props or blocks before disconnecting fixings — no item may be dismantled while only fastener-attached.
Use mechanical hoist, trolley, or mobile elevated work platform to lower items greater than 20 kg — hand-lowering is prohibited.
Barricade the work zone with tape and signage — no public or workers outside removal team within 3 metres.
Remove fasteners (screws, bolts, adhesive) with power tools or hand tools only — do not cut, grind, or create dust during disconnection.
Load items into skip bin via loading dock only — do not throw, drop, or slide items into bin.
Check underlying substrate for contamination, damage, or unexpected material before exposing to general work area — record condition and report defects before work area is handed back.
Wear cut-resistant gloves and closed-toe boots during all disconnection and handling tasks.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not load items into skip until: underlying substrate is checked and documented by site supervisor or project manager, and any defects or contamination requiring specialist attention are flagged
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: suspected or confirmed ACM is found in cabinetry, adhesive, sealant, or substrate finish — isolate area and tell licensed asbestos contractor immediately
🛑 STOP WORK if: any item tips, shifts, or begins to fall during removal or lowering — do not attempt to catch or stabilise; allow item to fall clear and reassess support method
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker stands on cabinetry, shelving, or unstable joinery to access fixings — use step ladder or elevated access equipment instead
admin: Brief all workers on asbestos risk and recognised ACM indicators before work starts — confirm understanding in writing or verbal acknowledgment recorded by supervisor.
Maintain daily site logbook recording substrate checks, any defects found, and confirmation of no ACM disturbance.
Do not allow public access to work zone — confirm adjacent areas (corridors, offices) are isolated or monitored throughout removal.
ppe: Dust mask P2 or organic vapour respirator if adhesive or sealant removal generates odour or mist (per SDS if applicable)
Fall arrest harness and lanyard (if standing on elevated or unstable surface to access fixings)

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Once at start of task. Substrate check once per item removed or at logical break point.
monitoring.evidence: Hazmat clearance certificate on site. Substrate inspection checklist signed off. Daily site logbook entry confirming no ACM disturbance and substrate condition noted.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove fixed joinery and built-in
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove fixed joinery and built-in per SWMS

tasks.task: Remove suspended ceiling system and soffit finishes
tasks.scope: Lower and dismantle suspended ceiling grid, acoustic panels, and associated ducting. Remove soffit finishes. Maintain falling-object exclusion zone. Check for asbestos in any insulation or lagging before removal.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker on ladder or elevated platform whilst removing grid or panels
Struck by falling ceiling components — grid section, panel, or duct hangers detach or drop
Asbestos fibre release — insulation, lagging, or fireproofing material in soffit disturbed without containment
Electrical shock — contact with recessed lights or services embedded in ceiling during removal
tasks.dominant_hazard: Struck by falling ceiling components — grid section, panel, or duct hangers detach or drop
controls: Establish exclusion zone 3 m radius below all ceiling removal work. Prohibit unauthorised entry. Post warning signs at all entry points.
If asbestos is confirmed present, engage Class A licensed asbestos contractor. Do not proceed with removal using in-house labour.
Isolate all electrical circuits serving recessed lights and embedded services before work starts. Verify isolation at point of work with multimeter. Tag isolated breakers 'Do Not Switch On'.
Use scaffold tower or mobile elevated work platform (MEWP) for all ceiling-height work. Do not use ladder as primary access for grid or panel removal.
Secure ceiling grid sections to scaffold before lowering. Lower sections in controlled manner using rope and pulley. Do not drop or allow free fall of components.
Brief all workers on asbestos identification (white or grey lagging, loose-fill insulation around ducts). Show photographs of suspect materials. Stop work if any suspected asbestos is found.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start ceiling or soffit removal until: Asbestos assessment report is on-site, reviewed, and clearance confirmed by Site Supervisor
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: Any suspected asbestos material (white/grey lagging, loose-fill insulation) is encountered — do not disturb; tell supervisor immediately
🛑 STOP WORK if: Exclusion zone is breached or unauthorized person enters removal area
admin: If asbestos is confirmed, tell SafeWork NSW and engage Class A licensed asbestos removal contractor. Do not proceed in-house.
Site Supervisor to monitor exclusion zone continuously. Record daily entry/exit logs.
ppe: Organic vapour mask (AS 1716 P2) — if dust or chemical residue visible
Disposable coveralls — if asbestos-free but dust generation expected

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before work starts, and continuously during removal if any new suspect material is visible
monitoring.evidence: Signed clearance letter retained on-site; daily tool-box talk record confirming asbestos briefing; photographic record of exclusion zone signage and isolation tags

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove suspended ceiling system and
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove suspended ceiling system and per SWMS

tasks.task: Remove floor coverings and substrate preparation
tasks.scope: Remove carpet, timber, vinyl, and underlay. Undertake substrate clean and preparation. Confirm all ACM removal and service disconnection complete before occupant handover.
hazards: Trip or slip hazard — loosened carpet, vinyl, or underlay creating uneven surface
Dust inhalation — vinyl, carpet backing, or underlay dust during removal and vacuum
Skin irritation or chemical exposure — adhesives or treatments on backing not identified
ACM disturbance — if any asbestos-containing vinyl or adhesive not removed in Task 3
tasks.dominant_hazard: Dust inhalation — vinyl, carpet backing, or underlay dust during removal and vacuum
controls: Wet suppression: dampen carpet and underlay with clean water before cutting and removal to prevent dust liberation.
Use HEPA-filtered dust extraction at point of removal — connect extractor to cutting tool or handheld unit during carpet, vinyl, and underlay separation.
Wear organic vapour respirator (AS/NZS 1716 Half-mask P2 + cartridge) during removal if adhesive odour or vinyl off-gassing detected.
Barricade work area with plastic sheeting and seal gaps to exclude dust and fumes from adjacent spaces.
Prohibit dry sweeping or vacuuming of floor residue — use damp wiping or wet-extraction vacuum only.
Confirm ACM removal and service disconnection completion before starting floor covering removal — hold point authority to sign handover checklist.
After removal, damp wipe all exposed substrate with clean cotton cloths — dispose of all dust-bearing waste in sealed bags labelled 'asbestos precaution'.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove floor coverings until: ACM removal completion and service disconnection confirmed in writing by licensed asbestos removalist and Project Manager
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start substrate preparation until: substrate checked and signed off by supervisor confirming no visible contamination or unknown adhesive residue
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: vinyl backing, carpet underlay, or adhesive dust escapes work area barricade or dust extraction fails
🛑 STOP WORK if: asbestos-containing adhesive, vinyl, or backing material is discovered during removal
🛑 STOP WORK if: workers show respiratory symptoms, coughing, or shortness of breath during or immediately after removal
admin: Obtain written confirmation from licensed asbestos removalist (Class A or B) that all ACM removal is complete and site is clear — file before handover.
tell SafeWork NSW of asbestos removal work commencement and completion (WHS Reg 2017 Part 8.3).
Conduct air monitoring during removal if any friable asbestos material suspected — engage licensed air monitor; results must be below NOEL before handover.
Maintain asbestos removal register — record removal date, material type, licensee name, and disposal certificate.
Brief all site personnel (including occupant representatives) on asbestos precaution protocols and barricade restrictions before work starts.
ppe: Organic vapour respirator (AS/NZS 1716 Half-mask P2 + activated carbon cartridge) — required if adhesive or vinyl vapour detected
Disposable coveralls (Type 5) — wear during removal and substrate wiping

monitoring.critical_control: HEPA dust extraction running continuously — check airflow and filter integrity at start and every 2 hours.
monitoring.who: Supervisor and workers on point of use
monitoring.frequency: Before removal starts, every 2 hours during removal, before and after vacuum completion
monitoring.evidence: Visual airflow check, filter pressure gauge reading, dust bag integrity check, asbestos register entry, air monitoring certificate (if friable material encountered)

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove floor coverings and substrate
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove floor coverings and substrate per SWMS

tasks.task: Clear debris and load remaining waste into skip bins
tasks.scope: Consolidate all demolition waste and off-cuts. Load via loading dock into skip bins. Sweep and vacuum to remove dust and residual material. Floor ready for final inspection.
hazards: Manual handling strain — lifting heavy debris or off-cuts into skip bins without mechanical aid
Puncture or laceration — stepping on or handling nails, glass, or sharp edges in debris
Struck by falling debris — overloaded skip bin or unstable stack shifting during loading
Dust inhalation — sweeping and vacuuming without respiratory protection
tasks.dominant_hazard: Manual handling strain — lifting heavy debris or off-cuts into skip bins without mechanical aid
controls: Segregate debris by weight category before loading — heavy items (>15 kg) to be moved mechanically or in pairs.
Use mechanical handling equipment (trolley, pallet jack, or crane) to move heavy debris and off-cuts to skip bin — no manual lift above shoulder height.
check skip bin base for stability and correct positioning before loading — confirm bin is level and supported on firm ground.
Fill skip bin from bottom; do not stack debris above bin rim — overloading creates fall risk.
Scan debris for nails, glass, and sharp edges before handling — remove or cover protruding hazards with tape.
Wear cut-resistant gloves and steel-capped boots during debris handling and loading.
Vacuum or damp-sweep floor after each loading cycle — suppress dust with water spray before sweeping.
Do not dry sweep — use damp cloth or HEPA-filtered vacuum to capture fine dust and residual material.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start final floor inspection until: all debris has been removed, vacuum or damp-sweep completed, and no visible dust or residual material remains on floor surface.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: skip bin becomes overloaded, unstable, or begins to shift during loading.
🛑 STOP WORK if: mechanical handling equipment becomes unavailable and heavy debris (>15 kg) requires manual lift.
🛑 STOP WORK if: dust suppression fails during sweeping or vacuuming and visibility is reduced or respiratory irritation occurs.
admin: Assign nominated loader and spotter — spotter to monitor bin stability and exclusion zone during each load cycle.
Brief all workers on location of skip bins, loading sequence, and mechanical equipment operation before work starts.
Record debris removal completion and floor condition sign-off in site diary — document any unexpected waste type or volume.
ppe: Organic vapour respirator (P2 or equivalent) if solvent odour present during sweeping
Eye protection if vacuuming generates dust cloud

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before each loading cycle and before final inspection
monitoring.evidence: Visual check and site diary entry — bin condition logged, debris category recorded, floor cleanliness confirmed by torch inspection

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Clear debris and load remaining
responsibility.WKR: Perform Clear debris and load remaining per SWMS

tasks.task: Confirm site readiness and establish site control
tasks.scope: Verify building access, utility disconnection sign-off, asbestos survey report on-site, skip bin placement via loading dock confirmed, exclusion zone established below demolition face.
hazards: Utility isolation not confirmed — contact with live electrical or gas
Asbestos survey report missing or incomplete — hidden ACM not identified before removal
Skip bin placement blocking emergency egress or pedestrian route
tasks.dominant_hazard: Utility isolation not confirmed — contact with live electrical or gas
controls: Obtain written utility disconnection sign-off from service provider (Ausgrid / APA / water authority) naming each service and disconnection date before site access commences.
Verify skip bin placed via loading dock and does not obstruct emergency egress, stairwells, fire exits, or public pedestrian routes.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: utility disconnection sign-off cannot be obtained or is incomplete — contact service provider and obtain written confirmation before proceeding.
🛑 STOP WORK if: asbestos survey report is missing, incomplete, or assessment is older than 12 months — obtain updated survey by licensed assessor.
🛑 STOP WORK if: skip bin obstructs emergency egress, fire exit, or public pedestrian route — move bin via loading dock or alternative approved route.
admin: Obtain asbestos removal permit (where required by local council) and display on-site.
Maintain site induction register recording date, worker name, licence verification, and sign-off for site readiness confirmation.

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled
monitoring.frequency: Before site access commences — once only
monitoring.evidence: Written sign-off from service provider (Ausgrid / APA / water authority) filed in site documentation; asbestos survey report date-stamped and filed on-site.

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

tasks.task: Conduct final inspection and handover
tasks.scope: Verify all demolition complete, services isolated and capped, exclusion zone removed, waste removed, floor clean. Obtain client sign-off before demobilisation.
hazards: Missed asbestos or hazardous material — incomplete identification or removal not detected before handover
Utilities not isolated or capped — live electrical, gas, or water hazard remains in ceiling or walls
Exclusion zone not properly removed — residual contamination or tripping hazard persists
Debris or dust not cleared — slip, trip, or inhalation hazard on clean floor
tasks.dominant_hazard: Missed asbestos or hazardous material — incomplete identification or removal not detected before handover
controls: Verify all service caps and isolation points — electrical isolators locked off, gas taps capped, water mains shut and capped, drainage capped — and photograph each.
Remove all exclusion zone signage, tape, and temporary barriers only after debris removal is complete and floor is visibly clear.
Vacuum floor using HEPA filter unit and damp-wipe all horizontal surfaces to remove residual dust. Do not dry sweep.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not demobilise until: client has completed final inspection with site supervisor, confirmed no defects or residual hazards remain, and signed project handover register.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any unknown friable or suspect asbestos material is discovered during final walk — tell supervisor and licensed assessor immediately.
🛑 STOP WORK if: floor or horizontal surfaces contain visible debris, dust accumulation, or evidence of residual contamination after vacuum and wipe.
admin: Confirm asbestos removal permit and disposal certificates are attached to project file and available for client review.
Confirm air monitoring results (if Class A removal was conducted) are on file and within acceptable clearance limits.
Complete project defects register with client signature. Record any minor non-compliance items and remediation method.
Confirm all waste removal dockets and asbestos disposal certificates are filed before demobilisation sign-off.
ppe: P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) mask (if dust disturbance during final vacuum is anticipated)

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled
monitoring.who: Site Supervisor and Licensed Asbestos Assessor
monitoring.frequency: Once, before client handover
monitoring.evidence: Asbestos removal completion certificate, air monitoring report (if Class A), disposal dockets, signed project handover register, and photographs of service isolation points and clean floor

responsibility.SUP: Supervise dismantling and demobilisation, verify controls, manage site access
responsibility.WKR: Dismantle and clear per SWMS, report hazards, obey spotter directions

tasks.task: Demobilise equipment and site restoration
tasks.scope: Remove temporary barriers, signage, and site protection. Return site to safe-access state. Remove all plant and equipment from site.
hazards: Trip or fall hazard — temporary barriers, signage, or protection materials left in place or stacked unstably
Manual handling strain — removing or stacking heavy barriers or site protection panels
Residual contamination — asbestos dust or debris not fully cleaned from equipment or floor during removal
tasks.dominant_hazard: Trip or fall hazard — temporary barriers, signage, or protection materials left in place or stacked unstably
controls: Before removing any barrier or protection panel, photograph its position and condition to confirm no asbestos dust or settled debris on or beneath it.
Damp-wipe all temporary barriers, signage, and protection panels with wet cloth before stacking or moving to remove settled dust.
Stack barriers and panels against a fixed wall or frame — maximum 1.5 m height, stable base — do not lean against temporary supports.
Remove signage, warning tape, and rope exclusions before removing physical barriers; roll tape tightly and place in sealed skip.
Clear all floor and access routes of protection materials, offcuts, debris, and trip hazards; sweep and damp-wipe final surface.
Load equipment and barriers onto vehicle in order: heaviest items first, lightest on top; secure load with restraint straps.
Two workers minimum for each barrier or panel weighing over 25 kg; use mechanical lifting aid (trolley, slide sheet) where available.
Check floor beneath removed barriers for asbestos dust, debris, or staining; damp-wipe if present; photograph final condition.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove barriers or protection until: asbestos removal contractor or licensed supervisor confirms all friable and non-friable material has been removed and final clearance air monitoring is complete (if Class A work was performed)
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not demobilise equipment until: site supervisor confirms floor is clear of debris, trip hazards, and contamination; all barriers documented as removed
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: asbestos dust, fibres, or settled contamination is visible on floor, equipment, or barriers during removal
🛑 STOP WORK if: barriers or panels cannot be safely stacked or removed without manual strain injury risk; call mechanical handling support
🛑 STOP WORK if: floor surface shows signs of contamination, staining, or unknown material after barrier removal — obtain licensed assessor inspection before proceeding
admin: Obtain final air-clearance certificate from licensed air-monitoring contractor before demobilisation commences (if Class A asbestos removal was performed on site).

task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Dust inhalation — silica or asbestos dust from cutting or demolition not suppressed
controls: Wet-cut all partition wall sections and studs. Use water spray to suppress dust continuously during cutting. No dry breakout permitted.
Check for hidden services (power, water, gas) at each cut point using thermal imaging, utility locator, or architect plan before power saw or reciprocating saw starts.
Wear organic vapour + particulate respirator (P2 cartridge + organic vapour cartridge per SDS) during all dry debris handling or re-entry to dust zone.
Wear eye protection, heavy-duty cut-resistant gloves, and steel-capped boots during wall removal and debris handling.
Load debris into skip bin from platform or ground level only. Do not throw from height. Segregate asbestos or asbestos-suspect material into separate skip or sealed bag immediately.
Use harness and lanyard (anchor to fixed structure above, tested safe for load) when cutting from ladder or elevated platform above 2 m. Do not work alone.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not load debris from height until: exclusion zone is confirmed clear of personnel, skip bin position is stable and level, and wet suppression or dust containment is in place
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet suppression system fails, water spray stops, or dry cutting occurs — do not resume until water supply is restored and dust has settled
🛑 STOP WORK if: hidden service is struck, identified, or suspected (electrical outlet, pipe, conduit) — isolate immediately, tell site supervisor, do not touch or cut further
🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion zone is breached by unauthorised personnel, debris escapes containment, or air quality cannot be maintained
admin: Obtain and display Asbestos Removal Permit (if Class A asbestos confirmed) before any licensed removal work starts.
Arrange independent air monitoring during all Class A asbestos removal work. Provide results to SafeWork NSW within prescribed timeframe.
Brief all site personnel on exclusion zone boundaries, RPE requirements, and stop-work triggers before work starts.
Maintain disposal certificates for all asbestos waste. Arrange licensed asbestos waste contractor for removal and burial at approved facility.
Provide Site Induction and SWMS walkthrough to all workers before tool issue. Confirm understanding in writing.
ppe: Organic vapour + particulate respirator (P2 cartridge + organic vapour cartridge per SDS) — wear during cutting, demolition, and dry debris handling
eye protection— during cutting, demolition, and debris loading
Steel-capped boots — on site always during demolition
hi-viz shirt or vest— during all work in exclusion zone
High-visibility vest — for visibility below active demolition face

monitoring.critical_control: Verify water spray is active and continuous during all cutting. Check dust visible in air — if present, stop and increase water pressure.
monitoring.frequency: Before each cut and continuous during cutting
monitoring.evidence: Water supply connected and flowing visibly; air quality observed clear; exclusion zone barricade remains intact; no personnel without RPE in zone

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove partition walls and framing
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove partition walls and framing per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Remove suspended ceiling system and soffit finishes
task_blocks_raw.scope: Lower and dismantle suspended ceiling grid, acoustic panels, and associated ducting. Remove soffit finishes. Maintain falling-object exclusion zone. Check for asbestos in any insulation or lagging before removal.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker on ladder or elevated platform whilst removing grid or panels
Struck by falling ceiling components — grid section, panel, or duct hangers detach or drop
Asbestos fibre release — insulation, lagging, or fireproofing material in soffit disturbed without containment
Electrical shock — contact with recessed lights or services embedded in ceiling during removal
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Struck by falling ceiling components — grid section, panel, or duct hangers detach or drop
controls: Establish exclusion zone 3 m radius below all ceiling removal work. Prohibit unauthorised entry. Post warning signs at all entry points.
If asbestos is confirmed present, engage Class A licensed asbestos contractor. Do not proceed with removal using in-house labour.
Isolate all electrical circuits serving recessed lights and embedded services before work starts. Verify isolation at point of work with multimeter. Tag isolated breakers 'Do Not Switch On'.
Use scaffold tower or mobile elevated work platform (MEWP) for all ceiling-height work. Do not use ladder as primary access for grid or panel removal.
Secure ceiling grid sections to scaffold before lowering. Lower sections in controlled manner using rope and pulley. Do not drop or allow free fall of components.
Brief all workers on asbestos identification (white or grey lagging, loose-fill insulation around ducts). Show photographs of suspect materials. Stop work if any suspected asbestos is found.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start ceiling or soffit removal until: Asbestos assessment report is on-site, reviewed, and clearance confirmed by Site Supervisor
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: Any suspected asbestos material (white/grey lagging, loose-fill insulation) is encountered — do not disturb; tell supervisor immediately
🛑 STOP WORK if: Exclusion zone is breached or unauthorized person enters removal area
admin: If asbestos is confirmed, tell SafeWork NSW and engage Class A licensed asbestos removal contractor. Do not proceed in-house.
Site Supervisor to monitor exclusion zone continuously. Record daily entry/exit logs.
ppe: Organic vapour mask (AS 1716 P2) — if dust or chemical residue visible
Disposable coveralls — if asbestos-free but dust generation expected

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before work starts, and continuously during removal if any new suspect material is visible
monitoring.evidence: Signed clearance letter retained on-site; daily tool-box talk record confirming asbestos briefing; photographic record of exclusion zone signage and isolation tags

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove suspended ceiling system and
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove suspended ceiling system and per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Remove floor coverings and substrate preparation
task_blocks_raw.scope: Remove carpet, timber, vinyl, and underlay. Undertake substrate clean and preparation. Confirm all ACM removal and service disconnection complete before occupant handover.
hazards: Trip or slip hazard — loosened carpet, vinyl, or underlay creating uneven surface
Dust inhalation — vinyl, carpet backing, or underlay dust during removal and vacuum
Skin irritation or chemical exposure — adhesives or treatments on backing not identified
ACM disturbance — if any asbestos-containing vinyl or adhesive not removed in Task 3
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Dust inhalation — vinyl, carpet backing, or underlay dust during removal and vacuum
controls: Wet suppression: dampen carpet and underlay with clean water before cutting and removal to prevent dust liberation.
Use HEPA-filtered dust extraction at point of removal — connect extractor to cutting tool or handheld unit during carpet, vinyl, and underlay separation.
Wear organic vapour respirator (AS/NZS 1716 Half-mask P2 + cartridge) during removal if adhesive odour or vinyl off-gassing detected.
Barricade work area with plastic sheeting and seal gaps to exclude dust and fumes from adjacent spaces.
Prohibit dry sweeping or vacuuming of floor residue — use damp wiping or wet-extraction vacuum only.
Confirm ACM removal and service disconnection completion before starting floor covering removal — hold point authority to sign handover checklist.
After removal, damp wipe all exposed substrate with clean cotton cloths — dispose of all dust-bearing waste in sealed bags labelled 'asbestos precaution'.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove floor coverings until: ACM removal completion and service disconnection confirmed in writing by licensed asbestos removalist and Project Manager
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start substrate preparation until: substrate checked and signed off by supervisor confirming no visible contamination or unknown adhesive residue
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: vinyl backing, carpet underlay, or adhesive dust escapes work area barricade or dust extraction fails
🛑 STOP WORK if: asbestos-containing adhesive, vinyl, or backing material is discovered during removal
🛑 STOP WORK if: workers show respiratory symptoms, coughing, or shortness of breath during or immediately after removal
admin: Obtain written confirmation from licensed asbestos removalist (Class A or B) that all ACM removal is complete and site is clear — file before handover.
tell SafeWork NSW of asbestos removal work commencement and completion (WHS Reg 2017 Part 8.3).
Conduct air monitoring during removal if any friable asbestos material suspected — engage licensed air monitor; results must be below NOEL before handover.
Maintain asbestos removal register — record removal date, material type, licensee name, and disposal certificate.
Brief all site personnel (including occupant representatives) on asbestos precaution protocols and barricade restrictions before work starts.
ppe: Organic vapour respirator (AS/NZS 1716 Half-mask P2 + activated carbon cartridge) — required if adhesive or vinyl vapour detected
Disposable coveralls (Type 5) — wear during removal and substrate wiping

monitoring.critical_control: HEPA dust extraction running continuously — check airflow and filter integrity at start and every 2 hours.
monitoring.who: Supervisor and workers on point of use
monitoring.frequency: Before removal starts, every 2 hours during removal, before and after vacuum completion
monitoring.evidence: Visual airflow check, filter pressure gauge reading, dust bag integrity check, asbestos register entry, air monitoring certificate (if friable material encountered)

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove floor coverings and substrate
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove floor coverings and substrate per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Clear debris and load remaining waste into skip bins
task_blocks_raw.scope: Consolidate all demolition waste and off-cuts. Load via loading dock into skip bins. Sweep and vacuum to remove dust and residual material. Floor ready for final inspection.
hazards: Manual handling strain — lifting heavy debris or off-cuts into skip bins without mechanical aid
Puncture or laceration — stepping on or handling nails, glass, or sharp edges in debris
Struck by falling debris — overloaded skip bin or unstable stack shifting during loading
Dust inhalation — sweeping and vacuuming without respiratory protection
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Manual handling strain — lifting heavy debris or off-cuts into skip bins without mechanical aid
controls: Segregate debris by weight category before loading — heavy items (>15 kg) to be moved mechanically or in pairs.
Use mechanical handling equipment (trolley, pallet jack, or crane) to move heavy debris and off-cuts to skip bin — no manual lift above shoulder height.
check skip bin base for stability and correct positioning before loading — confirm bin is level and supported on firm ground.
Fill skip bin from bottom; do not stack debris above bin rim — overloading creates fall risk.
Scan debris for nails, glass, and sharp edges before handling — remove or cover protruding hazards with tape.
Wear cut-resistant gloves and steel-capped boots during debris handling and loading.
Vacuum or damp-sweep floor after each loading cycle — suppress dust with water spray before sweeping.
Do not dry sweep — use damp cloth or HEPA-filtered vacuum to capture fine dust and residual material.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start final floor inspection until: all debris has been removed, vacuum or damp-sweep completed, and no visible dust or residual material remains on floor surface.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: skip bin becomes overloaded, unstable, or begins to shift during loading.
🛑 STOP WORK if: mechanical handling equipment becomes unavailable and heavy debris (>15 kg) requires manual lift.
🛑 STOP WORK if: dust suppression fails during sweeping or vacuuming and visibility is reduced or respiratory irritation occurs.
admin: Assign nominated loader and spotter — spotter to monitor bin stability and exclusion zone during each load cycle.
Brief all workers on location of skip bins, loading sequence, and mechanical equipment operation before work starts.
Record debris removal completion and floor condition sign-off in site diary — document any unexpected waste type or volume.
ppe: Organic vapour respirator (P2 or equivalent) if solvent odour present during sweeping
Eye protection if vacuuming generates dust cloud

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before each loading cycle and before final inspection
monitoring.evidence: Visual check and site diary entry — bin condition logged, debris category recorded, floor cleanliness confirmed by torch inspection

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Clear debris and load remaining
responsibility.WKR: Perform Clear debris and load remaining per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.scope: Verify all demolition complete, services isolated and capped, exclusion zone removed, waste removed, floor clean. Obtain client sign-off before demobilisation.
hazards: Missed asbestos or hazardous material — incomplete identification or removal not detected before handover
Utilities not isolated or capped — live electrical, gas, or water hazard remains in ceiling or walls
Exclusion zone not properly removed — residual contamination or tripping hazard persists
Debris or dust not cleared — slip, trip, or inhalation hazard on clean floor
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Missed asbestos or hazardous material — incomplete identification or removal not detected before handover
controls: Verify all service caps and isolation points — electrical isolators locked off, gas taps capped, water mains shut and capped, drainage capped — and photograph each.
Remove all exclusion zone signage, tape, and temporary barriers only after debris removal is complete and floor is visibly clear.
Vacuum floor using HEPA filter unit and damp-wipe all horizontal surfaces to remove residual dust. Do not dry sweep.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not demobilise until: client has completed final inspection with site supervisor, confirmed no defects or residual hazards remain, and signed project handover register.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any unknown friable or suspect asbestos material is discovered during final walk — tell supervisor and licensed assessor immediately.
🛑 STOP WORK if: floor or horizontal surfaces contain visible debris, dust accumulation, or evidence of residual contamination after vacuum and wipe.
admin: Confirm asbestos removal permit and disposal certificates are attached to project file and available for client review.
Confirm air monitoring results (if Class A removal was conducted) are on file and within acceptable clearance limits.
Complete project defects register with client signature. Record any minor non-compliance items and remediation method.
Confirm all waste removal dockets and asbestos disposal certificates are filed before demobilisation sign-off.
ppe: P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) mask (if dust disturbance during final vacuum is anticipated)

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled
monitoring.who: Site Supervisor and Licensed Asbestos Assessor
monitoring.frequency: Once, before client handover
monitoring.evidence: Asbestos removal completion certificate, air monitoring report (if Class A), disposal dockets, signed project handover register, and photographs of service isolation points and clean floor

responsibility.SUP: Supervise dismantling and demobilisation, verify controls, manage site access
responsibility.WKR: Dismantle and clear per SWMS, report hazards, obey spotter directions

task_blocks_raw.scope: Remove temporary barriers, signage, and site protection. Return site to safe-access state. Remove all plant and equipment from site.
hazards: Trip or fall hazard — temporary barriers, signage, or protection materials left in place or stacked unstably
Manual handling strain — removing or stacking heavy barriers or site protection panels
Residual contamination — asbestos dust or debris not fully cleaned from equipment or floor during removal
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Trip or fall hazard — temporary barriers, signage, or protection materials left in place or stacked unstably
controls: Before removing any barrier or protection panel, photograph its position and condition to confirm no asbestos dust or settled debris on or beneath it.
Damp-wipe all temporary barriers, signage, and protection panels with wet cloth before stacking or moving to remove settled dust.
Stack barriers and panels against a fixed wall or frame — maximum 1.5 m height, stable base — do not lean against temporary supports.
Remove signage, warning tape, and rope exclusions before removing physical barriers; roll tape tightly and place in sealed skip.
Clear all floor and access routes of protection materials, offcuts, debris, and trip hazards; sweep and damp-wipe final surface.
Load equipment and barriers onto vehicle in order: heaviest items first, lightest on top; secure load with restraint straps.
Two workers minimum for each barrier or panel weighing over 25 kg; use mechanical lifting aid (trolley, slide sheet) where available.
Check floor beneath removed barriers for asbestos dust, debris, or staining; damp-wipe if present; photograph final condition.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove barriers or protection until: asbestos removal contractor or licensed supervisor confirms all friable and non-friable material has been removed and final clearance air monitoring is complete (if Class A work was performed)
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not demobilise equipment until: site supervisor confirms floor is clear of debris, trip hazards, and contamination; all barriers documented as removed
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: asbestos dust, fibres, or settled contamination is visible on floor, equipment, or barriers during removal
🛑 STOP WORK if: barriers or panels cannot be safely stacked or removed without manual strain injury risk; call mechanical handling support
🛑 STOP WORK if: floor surface shows signs of contamination, staining, or unknown material after barrier removal — obtain licensed assessor inspection before proceeding
admin: Obtain final air-clearance certificate from licensed air-monitoring contractor before demobilisation commences (if Class A asbestos removal was performed on site).
Confirm all temporary barricades and exclusion zones are formally closed and documented on project daily log.
Provide induction to demobilisation crew on asbestos contamination awareness and damp-wipe procedure before site entry.
Photodocument final site condition: barriers removed, floor clear, no contamination visible — retain images in project file.
Record demobilisation date, time, crew, and barriers/equipment removed in site diary; sign-off by site supervisor.
ppe: Organic vapour respirator if damp-wiping residual asbestos dust (APF 10 minimum; refer to SDS and SafeWork NSW Code of Practice Section 5)

monitoring.critical_control: Damp-wipe all barriers and check floor for visible asbestos dust or debris before and after removal; photograph condition.
monitoring.who: Licensed asbestos contractor (if Class A work performed); otherwise site supervisor and demobilisation crew
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during demobilisation; final check before crew exit
monitoring.evidence: Photographs of barrier condition pre- and post-removal; final air-clearance certificate (if Class A); site diary entry; supervisor sign-off on floor condition

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues
